'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****The [[Taliban]] captures the eastern [[Logar Province]] and seizes seven more [[Provinces of Afghanistan|provincial]] capitals, [[Gardez]], [[Sharana]], [[Asadabad, Afghanistan|Asadabad]], [[Maymana]], [[Mihtarlam]], [[Nili, Afghanistan|Nili]] and [[Mazar-i-Sharif]], as heavy fighting is reported amid a rapid advance of the group towards the capital [[Kabul]]. Mazar-i-Sharif had been visited on Wednesday by [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/afghanistan-taliban-attack-mazar-e-sharif-live-updates/a-58863457 (Deutsche Welle)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/14/major-northern-afghan-city-mazar-i-sharif-falls-to-the-taliban (Al Jazeera)]
****President Ghani addresses the nation and says that he is in "urgent talks" with local leaders and international partners as the Taliban advances closer to Kabul. Ghani did not comment on the Taliban's demand that he resign in order to restore talks. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-troops-arrive-afghan-capital-assist-evacuations-2021-08-14/ (Reuters)]
****[[Embassy of the United States, Kabul|U.S. diplomatic staff]] and [[Western world|western]] nationals are [[airlift]]ed out of a heavily fortified part of Kabul. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/aug/14/us-troops-start-to-arrive-for-afghanistan-evacuation-as-taliban-close-in-on-kabul (''The Guardian'')] 
****It is reported that the Taliban has reached the outskirts of [[Kabul]] as the government seeks to control the city as a last stronghold. [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/business/article253489254.html (''Miami Herald'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-troops-arrive-afghan-capital-assist-evacuations-2021-08-14/ (Reuters)]
****Taliban forces seize the palace of U.S.-backed Afghan [[warlord]] [[Abdul Rashid Dostum]] in [[Mazar-i-Sharif]] amid reports that the warlord had left the country. Former warlord and [[List of governors of Balkh|Governor of Balkh]] [[Atta Muhammad Nur]] had also left the country, according to reports. [https://nation.lk/online/rampant-taliban-ransack-the-palatial-home-of-top-afghan-warlord-and-us-ally-general-dostum-110887.html (''The Nation'')]
****For the first time since the offensive began, the Taliban commandeers [[Mil Mi-17|Mi-17]] helicopters captured from the [[Afghan Air Force]]. The militants were filmed flying the aircraft over the city of [[Kandahar]]. The [[Jihadism|jihadist]] group has also seized several [[Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk|UH-60 Black Hawk]] helicopters. [https://www.msn.com/en-gb/news/world/taliban-seize-control-of-afghan-government-s-mi-17-helicopters/vi-AANk0aR (MSN)]
**[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Joe Biden]] authorizes the deployment of 5,000 [[United States Armed Forces|American troops]] to [[Afghanistan]] to help evacuate diplomatic staff and personnel. He reaffirms that the [[United States]] should end its 20-year presence in the country. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/biden-authorizes-5-000-troops-afghanistan-amid-taliban-advance-n1276840 (NBC News)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Twelve people are killed and more are wounded during a grenade attack against a truck carrying a family from a wedding ceremony in a [[Karachi]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/12-killed-in-overnight-grenade-attack-in-southern-pakistan/article35922584.ece (''The Hindu'')] 

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Haiti earthquake]]
**A major 7.2 magnitude [[earthquake]] strikes [[Petit Trou de Nippes]], [[Haiti]], killing at least 304 people and wounding more than 1,800 others. Several homes and buildings collapsed, with the earthquake being felt across the [[Caribbean]]. No [[tsunami warning]] has been issued. Haiti is still recovering from a [[2010 Haiti earthquake|major earthquake that impacted the country in 2010]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/magnitude-7-quake-strikes-western-haiti-usgs-2021-08-14/ (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58215631 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Turkish floods]]
**The death toll from the [[flash flood]]s in [[Kastamonu Province]] and [[Sinop, Turkey|Sinop]], [[Turkey]], increases to 57.  [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/14/turkey-flood-death-toll-hits-38 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Turkish wildfires]]
**A [[Beriev Be-200]], sent to help those affected by the wildfires in [[Kahramanmaraş]], crashes, killing all eight people on board, including five [[Russian Air Force|Russian servicemen]] and three [[Turkey|Turkish citizens]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/14/russian-firefighting-plane-crashes-in-southern-turkey (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Akkar explosion]]
**A [[Tank truck|fuel truck]] explodes in [[Akkar District]], [[Lebanon]], killing at least 28 people and injuring 79 others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/least-20-killed-lebanon-fuel-tank-explosion-mtv-news-2021-08-15/ (Reuters)]
*Eleven people are killed by the waves in the sea area off [[Zhangzhou]], [[Fujian]], [[China]]. [https://global.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202108/14/WS6117c811a310efa1bd668d01.html (''China Daily'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] announces a six-day general [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in all cities that will include the closure of [[bazaar]]s, markets, public offices, movie theaters, gyms and restaurants as well as a ban on intra-city travel. The lockdown will occur from August 16 to August 21. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/iran-will-impose-6-day-general-lockdown-over-coronavirus/amp/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] surpasses 30,000 deaths from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/coronavirus-cases-philippines-august-14-2021 (Rappler)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record 9,716 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 265,464. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/vietnam-reports-record-9716-new-covid-19-cases-2112836 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Denmark]] removes its mandatory [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face mask policy]] for public transport such as buses, trains or ferries, and also removes its recommendation of 1 meter of [[social distancing]] in public spaces. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/coronavirus-denmark-removes-last-of-its-obligatory-mask-rules-2509641 (NDTV)]
<!-- ***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 819 deaths from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 169,683. [https://floridanewstimes.com/russia-reports-virus-deaths-for-three-consecutive-days/324208/ (Florida News Times)] -->
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
****[[New South Wales]] enters a statewide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] which also applies to all [[Regions of New South Wales|regional parts of the state]] that are currently under a [[Stay-at-home order|stay-at-home]] order. All non-essential [[retail]] premises must close and all [[Hospitality industry|hospitality venue]]s will revert to [[Take-out|takeaway]] services after a record 466 new cases of COVID-19 were reported in the past 24 hours. [https://www.sbs.com.au/news/nsw-enters-statewide-lockdown-after-announcing-a-record-466-new-local-covid-19-cases (SBS World News)]
*[[Ivory Coast]] reports its first case of the [[Ebola]] hemorrhagic virus since 1994 in an isolated case of an 18-year-old girl who travelled from [[Guinea]] and is currently hospitalized in [[Abidjan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ivory-coast-detects-first-ebola-case-25-years-2021-08-14/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[BBC]] journalist [[Sarah Rainsford]] says that Russia is permanently expelling her after authorities told her to leave on Thursday. The expulsion is in response to two reporters from [[Mass media in Russia|Russian state-run news channel]] [[Russia-24]] being denied visas in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/bbc-reporter-says-russia-told-her-never-return-2021-08-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Zambian general election]]
**[[President of Zambia|President]] [[Edgar Lungu]] declares that Thursday's elections were "[[Free and fair election|not free or fair]]", citing instances of [[electoral violence]] in [[Provinces of Zambia|three provinces]], such as the beating of polling agents representing his party [[Patriotic Front (Zambia)|Patriotic Front]]. Early election results showed Lungu trailing behind his opponent, businessman [[Hakainde Hichilema]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/zambias-opposition-leader-hichilema-takes-early-presidential-election-lead-2021-08-14/ (Reuters)]
